_what: TRN-001 reproduction blockout spec (round 1: camera + blockout). Generic prayer-room feature wall; dims are the 2026-07-30 study's mutually-consistent spine (vault-grounded where the vault speaks, trade standards where it is silent). Committed file carries TRN-id + generic content only per qa/reproduction-curriculum.md.

light._what: 2026-07-31 round 4 (LIGHT). Every knob here is either a MEASUREMENT off the target or a declared inference — see downlights._measured. The round opened on trn001_lightcheck numbers, not on a look: our ceiling read 1.21x the wall against the target's 0.73x, our cubbies 1.63x too bright, our blacks 2.7x lifted, our frame's p99/p1 range 66:1 against 141:1, and our halo 1.92x too strong while clipping 2.15% of the frame against 0.08%. All five are one defect — rounds 1-3 lit the set with a WORLD, which lights a ceiling exactly as hard as a floor.
light._kelvin: 6000 K is a MEASUREMENT, bracketed at 5200/6200 against the target's own white surfaces: at 5200 our white wall read R/G 1.111 B/G 0.907 against the target's 1.050/0.951, at 6200 it read 1.060/0.976. The room still looks warm because the WOOD warms it, which is also why the target's ceiling (1.21/0.81, lit only by bounce off floor and header) is warmer than its walls (1.05/0.95) — our 3800 K first cut made every white surface in the room orange.
light._halo_w: bracketed against the glow band's ratio to the wall, not against how bright it looks: 16 gave 2.14x, 13 gave 2.22x, target is 1.72x. Pushing the strip deeper into the recess (setback 16 -> 45) was TESTED and moved it 2.223 -> 2.191, i.e. the halo's geometry is not the lever, its power is.

world._what: the world is not this room's light source — with the box closed it is only what leaks in. Rounds 1-3 ran it at 0.55 doing ALL the work, which is what made our ceiling as bright as our walls.

light._fill_refuted: 2026-07-31: an AREA light standing off frame on the camera side — the room's door/window — was BUILT and REFUTED by measurement, not by taste. The reasoning that led to it still stands (the target's floor ramps 42% toward frame-right while its ceiling shows no lean and its wall is brighter at the BOTTOM, which no ceiling fixture produces), but the source itself flattens the frame instead of ramping it: p99/p1 fell 50 -> 28 at 150 W and -> 15 at 400 W, while the floor tilt it was meant to create fell 21.7% -> 15.1% -> 7.1%. Recorded as an unresolved measurement like round 2's surround, NOT iterated (R1).

downlights._measured: x_mm and row_y_mm are MEASURED: the two lens discs were found as bright disks in the ceiling band and back-projected onto the ceiling plane z=2700, landing at (-999.5, -605.0) and (+1164.7, -605.5) — both 605 mm off the wall to within 0.5 mm, i.e. one wall-wash row. lens_dia_mm is the same probe read across the disc (86 and 91 mm). fill rows are INFERRED (the frame only shows the ceiling back to y~-880, so no second row is measurable) and use the measured column pitch as row pitch.
downlights._beam: THE PROFILE WAS CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT, from three real LM-63 files. Every remaining error after the level was right said one thing — our wall was over-washed — so the beam was too wide. 5.ies (Halo R-30 flood, 141 cd still at 40 deg) washed the wall from above and gave it the WRONG vertical shape; 30.IES (Kurt Versen C7394, medium) was better but flattened the frame to 32:1; 29.IES (Kurt Versen C7302, a real tight downlight, zero output past 45 deg) fixed four independent readings at once — cubby 0.051 vs 0.062 target, header 0.231 vs 0.252, the wall's top-to-bottom gradient flipped to the target's own shape, and the floor's falloff went 5.1% -> 23.6% against the target's 37.6%.

unit._surround_refuted: 2026-07-31: the 72mm proud-of-white-surface measurement is REAL and repeatable (stable across every tower depth tried), but the structure it implied — a furred-out white panel across the bay with the marble at the back of a 218mm reveal — was BUILT and the frame refuted it on sight: it reads as a deep TV niche, which the target is not. Recorded as an unresolved measurement, not built. Do not re-derive it from the same flank pixels without a new independent read.
unit._c2_round2: C2 round-2 triage 2026-07-31 (every item measured, none taken on taste): ACCEPTED+BUILT — shallow face (tower depth 360->80 from the 28px vs 101px side return, header 380->150, which also removes the phantom soffit joint the critic found under the header), altar radii to the measured 150-200mm family, centre box 900 wide at cx-25 and pedestals 268 at +/-772 (both were fat and shifted right), plinth toe 16/45 so the base shadow reads, left tower to floor so its underside stops showing, room wall closed to the unit edge at x=-1608. CARRIED — the target's lowest left cubby is SHORTER than its four siblings because the plinth cuts it (ours are equal); rounded TOP edges (a section bullnose, not a plan radius) are still square.
unit._depth_resolved: 2026-07-31, gate #2's carried question CLOSED by a third instrument. The built-in is ~100mm deep, not 360. Evidence: (A) the tower's inner side panel is one plane, so the depth making its front arris (u=459.3) and its wall junction (u=479.2) back-project to the same x is the depth -> 75mm; the earlier run missed this ONLY because its sweep started at 200. (B) a shelf board below the horizon shows its top surface as a band; the target's is 5.0px and the model gives 4/5/6px at cubby depth 80/100/120, while the old 342 gave 17.8px. (C) the critic's independent 28px-vs-101px side band. Why the landmark fit preferred 360: header_bot_* were the only landmarks whose 3D depended on tower depth, and their definition was wrong — a landmark defined wrongly returns a confident, precise, WRONG minimum. Same class as the rounded-silhouette trap; the lesson is that a fit can only test the geometry you told it about.
unit._owner_2026_07_31: owner spotted two things the builder missed: the side pedestals sat unequal because they were anchored to x=0 while the centre box sits off-centre — measured symmetric about the BOX at 705.1/704.3mm, so they now hang off the box; and the panel behind the Buddha is CONCEALED LIGHTING (ไฟซ่อน), not a lit surface — an LED strip hidden in the standoff gap behind the slab edge
unit._owner_base_reveal: owner 2026-07-31: the WOODEN BASE of the altar must project slightly further into the room than the blocks standing on it. Ours had the centre box overhanging its own base by 69mm — backwards for millwork. The step depth (311) is a direct VP-fitted measurement with 0.4px residuals, so it is the blocks that move: set back 26mm behind the base, with their widths re-read on the new silhouette plane and the measured symmetry about the box preserved.
unit._owner_flush_header: owner 2026-07-31: the tops of the two cubby stacks did not read level. Geometry was already symmetric, so the cause was the HEADER standing 30mm proud of the towers — its soffit overhangs each tower and, from an oblique camera, eats a different amount of each stack. The delivered piece keeps header and tower faces in one plane (the round-2 critic saw the same thing as a phantom joint line under our header). Header depth now derives from tower depth so the two can never drift apart again.

camera._solved: ROUND 4 CAUGHT THIS, and it is the class this project keeps paying for. The values below were the PRE-SOLVE VP estimate; the solved station lived only in a private scratch spec, so every gate frame from round 2 on was rendered from that file while the spec of record still said z=1150. Building round 4 from the spec of record therefore un-did round 1's camera solve — 83 mm of camera height, a ~40 px shift, landmark median 15.5 -> 54.6 px — and nothing failed, because a spec that renders is a spec that looks fine. The solved camera (which reproduces the round-3 gate frame to 0.00 px) now lives HERE, and a test refuses any spec whose camera lacks this marker, so a pre-solve camera can never sit in the spec of record again.
